title: Hosted spill attenuation and dedicated affinity escrow
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Teams have observed high variance in tail latency and cost when tenant traffic spills from dedicated GPU pools to the hosted fleet during sudden bursts or region outages. Current fallback is deterministic (dedicated-first, then immediately spill to hosted), which leads to cache-warmup penalties, model-variant mismatches, and uneven tenant cost exposure.

Goal:
Design and implement a middleware layer in the request router that attenuates hosted spill behavior and preserves tenant SLAs by: (1) introducing a short-lived 'affinity escrow' that keeps a tenant pinned to dedicated capacity where possible; (2) applying attenuation/damping to progressive spillover so we never fully evacuate a tenant without staged fallback steps; and (3) ensuring model-variant compatibility and KV-cache warmup strategies during transitions. The aim is to reduce P95/P99 latency regressions and customer-visible quality flips while limiting hosted cost delta.

Approach / Key components:
- Affinity escrow tokens: on heavy load, a tenant receives N escrow tokens that delay forced spillover for short intervals (configurable per tier). Tokens decay with time and are replenished by healthy dedicated capacity signals.
- Progressive attenuation: implement a spill attenuation coefficient (0..1) per tenant+region that reduces the probability of spill calls, ramping up only when dedicated node health is critically low.
- Grace routing path: three-step fallback path: (A) reduce batch size & degrade throughput on dedicated, (B) route <X% of requests to hosted for sampling + cache warmup, (C) full spill if capacity remains constrained for T seconds.
- Model variant safety: on hosted spill we prefer compatible model variants (quantized or lower-seq) with soft demotion instead of immediate variant swap; we also warm KV cache by sending synthetic prefetch calls derived from recent prefixes when allowed.
- Telemetry and circuit breakers: per-tenant counters for escrow usage, spill rate, latency delta, and hosted cost delta; automated circuit-breaker to force immediate failover to promoted variant if quality regression or token-rate exceeded.
- Console controls: expose attenuation coefficient and escrow window per tenant tier in Console (read-only until rollout 2).

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end flow covered by unit + e2e integration tests (router + orchestrator + runtime)
- P95 latency regression from spill events reduced by >= 30% on internal synthetic burst tests
- Hosted cost delta for sampled tenants limited to <10% during controlled experiments
- Rollout gated behind telemetry showing escrow token consumption and no customer-facing errors for 48h in canary region

Metrics to monitor:
- escrow_token_consumption_rate (per-tenant)
- spill_attempt_rate and successful_spill_rate
- latency_delta_hosted_vs_dedicated P50/P95/P99
- kv_cache_hit_rate_after_spill
- hosted_incurred_cost_delta_per_tenant

Runbook (short):
- If KPIs show increased quality regression: pause attenuation, revert to deterministic spill, open a P1 incident and notify SRE on-call.
- If escrow_token exhaustion for many tenants: investigate dedicated pool health, autoscale triggers, and capacity preemption logs.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Complexity vs predictability: escrow tokens add state and tuning knobs but avoid mass spill storms.
- Prefetching KV cache risks: synthetic prefetches can increase load and need safeguards; will be rate-limited and opt-in per-customer during initial rollouts.
- Cost vs latency: attenuation may slightly increase hosted cost in mid-term; we prefer measurable latency improvements before widening rollout.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Default escrow window per tier (proposal: P1 tenants 10s, P0 tenants 30s).
- Should we make prefetch synthetic calls billable to tenant or platform? Recommendation: platform-absorbed during initial trial.
- Policy authoring UX in Console (post-MVP).

ETA / Implementation phases:
- Phase 1 (2 sprints): router-side escrow tokens + progressive attenuation, unit tests, basic telemetry (canary region).
- Phase 2 (1 sprint): model-variant preference logic + KV-cache warmup hooks + integration tests.
- Phase 3 (1 sprint): Console exposure + rollout to additional regions + post-rollout analysis.

Notes:
This ticket focuses on routing policy logic; runtime-level kernel selection and quantization compatibility will be coordinated with runtime team (dependency ENG-13890). Must align with region affinity heuristics in ENG-41289.
